snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Science Hook: Mitochondria: Energy. Vit A: Eyes. Vit K: Clotting. Femur: Longest. Bacteria: TB. Mendel: Genetics.

quick_notes.title: Cell Biology
quick_notes.detail: Cell (Basic unit). Mitochondria (Powerhouse), Ribosomes (Protein factory), Nucleus (Control center).
quick_notes.explanation: A cell is the basic unit of life, meaning it is the smallest living part that makes up all plants and animals. Inside a cell, the mitochondria act as the powerhouse because they produce the energy the cell needs to work. The ribosomes are called the protein factory because they build proteins, which are essential for the cell's structure and function. The nucleus is the control center, as it holds the cell's DNA and directs all activities, like growth and reproduction.

quick_notes.title: Human Organs
quick_notes.detail: Liver (Largest gland), Skin (Largest organ), Femur (Longest bone), Stapes (Smallest bone).
quick_notes.explanation: The human body has several organs and structures with special size records. The liver is the largest gland in the body, meaning it is the biggest organ that produces and releases substances like bile to help digest food. The skin is the largest organ overall, covering and protecting the entire body. The femur, which is the thigh bone, is the longest and strongest bone in the body. The stapes, a tiny bone inside the ear, is the smallest bone in the body and helps you hear by vibrating when sound waves hit it.

quick_notes.title: Vitamins & Deficiency
quick_notes.detail: A (Night blindness), B1 (Beriberi), C (Scurvy), D (Rickets), K (Blood clotting failure).
quick_notes.explanation: Vitamins are substances your body needs in small amounts to work properly, and a deficiency means not having enough of a vitamin, which causes specific health problems. Vitamin A helps you see in dim light, and a deficiency leads to night blindness, where you cannot see well in low light. Vitamin B1 helps your nerves and heart, and a deficiency causes beriberi, which can damage nerves and cause weakness. Vitamin C keeps your blood vessels and gums healthy, and a deficiency causes scurvy, which leads to bleeding gums and slow wound healing. Vitamin D helps your body use calcium for strong bones, and a deficiency causes rickets, which makes bones soft and deformed in children. Vitamin K is needed for blood to clot, and a deficiency causes blood clotting failure, meaning even small cuts may bleed too much.

quick_notes.title: Diseases
quick_notes.detail: Bacterial (Cholera, TB, Typhoid), Viral (AIDS, Polio, Common cold), Fungal (Ringworm).
quick_notes.explanation: Diseases are health problems caused by tiny living things called germs. Bacteria are single-celled germs that can cause infections like cholera (severe diarrhea), tuberculosis or TB (a lung infection), and typhoid (a fever from contaminated food or water). Viruses are even smaller germs that need to get inside your body's cells to multiply; examples include AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome, caused by HIV), polio (which can cause paralysis), and the common cold (a mild nose and throat infection). Fungi are organisms like molds and yeasts that can cause infections such as ringworm, which is a skin

quick_notes.title: Genetics
quick_notes.detail: Father of Genetics: Gregor Mendel. DNA (Double helix - Watson & Crick (Double Helix structure, 1953) & Crick). 23 pairs of chromosomes.
quick_notes.explanation: Genetics is the study of how living things pass traits, like eye color or height, from parents to children. The father of genetics is Gregor Mendel, a scientist who discovered the basic rules of heredity, which is how traits are inherited. The most important molecule in genetics is DNA, which stands for Deoxyribonucleic Acid and carries all the genetic instructions.
